'''Rohini Godbole''' (12 November 1952<ref name="obituary"/> – 25 October 2024) was an Indian physicist and academic specializing in elementary particle physics: field theory and phenomenology.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nobelprizeseries.in/tbis/rgodbole|title=Rohini Godbole {{!}} The Best of Indian Science|website=nobelprizeseries.in|language=en|access-date=25 March 2018|archive-date=25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325171553/http://nobelprizeseries.in/tbis/rgodbole|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Rohini M Godbole {{!}} Rohini M Godbole|url=http://rmgodbole.in/|access-date=2021-03-06|language=en}}</ref> She was professor at the Centre for High Energy Physics, [[Indian Institute of Science]], [[Bangalore]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://chep.iisc.ac.in/Personnel/rohini.html|title=Prof. Rohini M. Godbole|website=chep.iisc.ac.in|publisher=Centre for High Energy Physics, IISc|access-date=25 March 2018|archive-date=22 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180322020012/http://chep.iisc.ac.in/Personnel/rohini.html|url-status=live}}</ref> She worked extensively on different aspects of particle phenomenology over three decades, in particular on exploring different aspects of the [[Standard Model of Particle Physics]] (SM) and the physics beyond it (BSM). Her work regarding hadronic structure of high-energy photons outlined a variety of ways in which to study it and has had implications for the design of next generation electron positron colliders. She was an elected fellow of all the three academies of Science of India and also the Science Academy of the Developing World (TWAS).<ref>{{cite web|title=Participant Details- India France Technology Summit 2013|url=http://www.indiafrancesummit.org/participants.php?action=view&id=791|access-date=4 April 2014|archive-date=7 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407075233/http://www.indiafrancesummit.org/participants.php?action=view&id=791|url-status=live}}</ref>

Apart from her work in academics, Godbole was also a much sought-after communicator of science, often delivering talks to young students, scholars and scientists on everything physics. She was also an avid supporter of women pursuing careers in science and technology, and along with Ram Ramaswamy, edited the book [[Lilavati's Daughters]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-features/tp-literaryreview/Forgotten-daughters/article15942107.ece|title=Forgotten daughters|date=2009-04-05|work=The Hindu|access-date=2018-03-25|language=en-IN|issn=0971-751X|archive-date=18 December 2019|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191218154214/https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-features/tp-literaryreview/Forgotten-daughters/article15942107.ece|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wMTxPgAACAAJ|title=Lilavati's Daughters: The Women Scientists of India|last1=Godbole|first1=Rohini M.|last2=Ramaswamy|first2=Ram|date=2008|publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences|isbn=978-81-8465-005-1|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.amazon.in/LILAVATIS-DAUGHTERS-Women-Scientists-India/dp/B00DT7E5UW|title=LILAVATI'S DAUGHTERS- The Women Scientists of India|last=Godbole|first=Rohini|editor-last=Ramaswamy|editor-first=Ram|access-date=25 March 2018|archive-date=25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325231956/https://www.amazon.in/LILAVATIS-DAUGHTERS-Women-Scientists-India/dp/B00DT7E5UW}}</ref> a collection of biographical essays on women scientists from India.

==Life and career==
Godbole was born in Pune, in the Indian state of Maharashtra in 1952. She graduated with a bachelor's degree in physics, mathematics and statistics from [[Sir Parshurambhau College]], University of Pune, and later obtained a masters in science degree from the [[Indian Institute of Technology Bombay|Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay]]. She completed here [[PhD]] in [[theoretical particle physics]] from the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Indian Fellow|url=http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P03-1334|access-date=29 March 2014|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140329110408/http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P03-1334|archive-date=29 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Rohini M Godbole |url=http://rmgodbole.in/|access-date=2021-03-06|language=en}}</ref>

Godbole joined [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]], Mumbai as a visiting fellow in 1979. She was Lecturer and Reader at the Department of Physics, University of Bombay from 1982 to 1995. She joined the Centre for High Energy Physics, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, as an associate professor in 1995 and has been a professor since June 1998. Superannuating there by 31 July 2021, she became an honorary professor.

She authored more than 150 research papers, many of which have some of the largest citation indices in her area.

Godbole died on 25 October 2024 at her home in Bangalore from a short-illness at the age of 71.<ref name="obituary">{{cite web |title=Noted physicist Rohini Godbole, a staunch advocate for Indian women in science, passes away |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/india/physicist-rohini-godbole-indian-women-science-passes-away-9638200/ |date=25 October 2024 | website=indianexpress.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/pune-news/renowned-physicist-gender-equity-proponent-rohini-godbole-dies-at-71-101729880612731.html|title=Renowned physicist, gender equity proponent Rohini Godbole dies at 71|publisher=Hindustan Times|date=27 October 2024|access-date=28 October 2024}}</ref>

==Research fields==
Godbole worked in the following areas-<ref>{{cite web|title=Rohini M. Godbole IISc Profile|url=http://cts.iisc.ernet.in/Personnel/pages/rohini/research/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130915110051/http://cts.iisc.ernet.in/Personnel/pages/rohini/research/index.html|archive-date=2013-09-15}}</ref> 
*New Particle Production at current and future colliders
*Physics at [[Large Hadron Collider]] and [[International Linear Collider|Next Linear Collider]]
*[[Quantum chromodynamics|QCD]] phenomenology: Structure Functions of a proton, photon and nucleus
*[[Supersymmetry]] and [[Electroweak interaction|Electroweak Physics]]

==Contribution==
Godbole was part of the International Detector Advisory Group (IDAG)<ref>{{cite web|title=International Detector Advisory Group (IDAG)|url=http://www.linearcollider.org/ILC/physics-detectors/Detectors/IDAG|access-date=29 March 2014|archive-date=31 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140331144320/http://www.linearcollider.org/ILC/physics-detectors/Detectors/IDAG|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Chasing the one trillion trillionth of a second|website=[[The Hindu]]|date=25 January 2012 |url=https://www.thehindu.com/life-and-style/money-and-careers/Chasing-the-one-trillion-trillionth-of-a-second/article13380698.ece|access-date=4 April 2014|archive-date=7 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407092453/http://www.thehindu.com/life-and-style/money-and-careers/chasing-the-one-trillion-trillionth-of-a-second/article2831537.ece|url-status=live}}</ref> for the [[International Linear Collider]] in the European research lab, [[CERN]]. The International Detector Advisory Group monitors the ILC detector research and development of the Research Directorate and the detector design groups. She was the Chair of the Panel for Women in Science initiative of the Indian Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{cite web|title=Women in Science- an Indian Academy of Sciences Initiative|url=http://www.ias.ac.in/womeninscience/|access-date=29 March 2014|archive-date=7 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407075047/http://www.ias.ac.in/womeninscience/|url-status=live}}</ref> Along with Ram Ramaswamy, Godbole jointly edited ''[[Lilavati's Daughters]]'', a collection of biographical essays on women scientists of India, which was published in the form of book by [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] in 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-features/tp-literaryreview/Forgotten-daughters/article15942107.ece|title=Forgotten daughters|work=The Hindu|date=4 April 2009 |access-date=27 May 2015|archive-date=30 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161030170235/http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-features/tp-literaryreview/forgotten-daughters/article662225.ece|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Books==
* ''Theory And Phenomenology Of Sparticles: An Account Of Four-dimensional N=1 Supersymmetry In High Energy Physics'':<ref>{{Cite book|title=Theory And Phenomenology Of Sparticles: An Account Of Four-dimensional N=1 Supersymmetry In High Energy Physics|date=2005-01-18|publisher=World Scientific Publishing Co Pte Ltd|isbn=978-981-256-531-0|editor-last=Drees|editor-first=Manuel|location=New Jersey|language=en|editor-last2=Godbole|editor-first2=Rohini|editor-last3=Roy|editor-first3=Probir}}</ref> Supersymmetry or SUSY, one of the most beautiful recent ideas of physics, predicts sparticles existing as superpartners of particles. This book gives a theoretical and phenomenological account of sparticles. Starting from a basic level, it provides a comprehensive, pedagogical and user-friendly treatment of the subject of four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetry as well as its observational aspects in high energy physics and cosmology.
* ''The Girl's Guide to a Life in Science'':<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.amazon.in/Girls-Guide-Life-Science-ebook/dp/B00TIPFLMA/ref=sr_1_2?s=books&ie=UTF8&qid=1521975557&sr=1-2|title=The Girl's Guide to a Life in Science|last=Ramaswamy|first=Ram|date=2015-02-11|publisher=Zubaan|editor-last=Godbole|editor-first=Rohini|language=en|editor-last2=Dubey|editor-first2=Mandakini|access-date=25 March 2018|archive-date=15 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115072943/https://www.amazon.in/Girls-Guide-Life-Science-ebook/dp/B00TIPFLMA/ref=sr_1_2?s=books&ie=UTF8&qid=1521975557&sr=1-2|url-status=live}}</ref> Inspiring, informative, ingenious...meet twenty-five of India's most celebrated female scientists. From astrophysics to zoology, learn what it takes to make a career in science. Who were they encouraged by? What did they struggle against? What motivated them to choose their particular field? What are the key questions at the cutting edge of modern research? What are the Big Questions that they are striving to find answers for? Why chose a life in science at all? Each of the women in this essential guide gives a short overview of their life and career. The profiles are accompanied by "Know-it-ology"—a brief introduction to their particular field of research. Each of the scientists describes her own "Eureka Moment". 
* ''LILAVATI'S DAUGHTERS- The Women Scientists of India (2008)''<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.amazon.in/LILAVATIS-DAUGHTERS-Women-Scientists-India/dp/B00DT7E5UW/ref=sr_1_3?s=books&ie=UTF8&qid=1521975557&sr=1-3|title=LILAVATI'S DAUGHTERS- The Women Scientists of India|last=Godbole|first=Rohini|date=January 2016 |publisher=Indian Academy Of Science |editor-last=Ramaswamy|editor-first=Ram}}{{Dead link|date=January 2021 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
